fields.description: Issue includes an editorial criticizing Florida Power & Light profits and advocating municipal acquisition of utility facilities; an investigative report alleging Browning King Co., Inc. sold damaged or inferior men’s clothing at high prices; and a major article linking Miami “Torture Doctor” T. Earl Moore to a pattern of patient harm and to the death of painter D. Kuhl. Additional pieces cover efforts to curb dog-track/summer racing and pari-mutuel gambling, a lawsuit over odors and nuisance from an Opa-locka broiler/slaughter plant, a report on segregation and job discrimination in Washington, D.C., statistics and development plans for Miami International Airport, and a letter from Florida’s new state superintendent of public instruction requesting press support for education.
